naming: A report is read by a strict reader over the YAML tree (YamlReportFlowLoader), not by a YamlDotNet deserializer: keys are case-sensitive and written exactly as listed here, an unknown key is a problem that keeps the document from loading, and every problem is reported with its line, all of them together. A key a running flow takes (schedule, mode, lifecycle, connections, server, source, target, load, onErrorResume) is refused with the reason: a report is a set of read-only queries a person runs from the report's page, and is never run as a flow. A parameter, a query and a column are named by the author: <parameter>, <query> and <column> stand for those names. A view is written under show as one mapping or as an entry of a list, so each view key is listed under both.

keys.description: The report's name: its identity in the estate and the pipeline row that holds its document. It is the heading of the report's page when no title is given. Plain text on one line, at most 400 characters.
keys.validation: Required. Missing, blank, over 400 characters, spanning several lines or holding a control character is a problem. A credential in the text is a problem; the value is never echoed in the message. A ${...} reference in the value is a problem: a report resolves its connection and nothing else, so the value is written plainly.

keys.description: The heading a person reads for the report. Left out, the report's name is shown. One line, at most 200 characters.
keys.validation: Over 200 characters, spanning several lines or holding a control character is a problem. A credential in the text is a problem; the value is never echoed in the message.

keys.description: What the report is for, in a sentence or two, shown with the report. It may span several lines. At most 1000 characters.
keys.validation: Over 1000 characters is a problem. A credential in the text is a problem; the value is never echoed in the message.

keys.description: A grouping label, as on every flow. Reports are listed by it, and it has no other effect: a report is never run, alone or with a batch. One line, at most 250 characters.
keys.validation: Over 250 characters, spanning several lines or holding a control character is a problem. A credential in the text is a problem; the value is never echoed in the message. A ${...} reference in the value is a problem: a report resolves its connection and nothing else, so the value is written plainly.

keys.description: The connection the report's queries run on; a query may name its own. It is written as one whole reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}) or an @alias, never as a connection string: a query runs on a worker, which is handed the reference to resolve and nothing else. The report is listed among what uses the connection. At most 512 characters.
keys.validation: Required: a report without it is a problem. A value that is not text, is blank or is over 512 characters is a problem. Anything that is not one whole reference or an @alias is a problem: a connection string, a reference with text around it, or an alias that holds a space, a ; or an =. The value is never echoed in the message, since a connection string may hold a credential.
